forecaster_note: Sat: chest high for most spots from the NE/E swell mix, a bit more push at S-facing with some longer S swell; light variable to N/NW winds in the morning are the cleanest window (still some wobble), then NE picks up — go S-facing. High tide first up: head for spots that handle some water. Sun: similar, chest to head high, N winds all day — S-facing cleanest. — Surfline forecaster, Sat 24 Oct

wind.summary: W 5 kph at 6am, WNW ~6 kph at 9am — glassy offshore. Turns ENE 12 kph by noon, ~19 kph (gust 24) arvo. Sunny, 18°C → ~25°C.

shark.summary: Tagged Bull Shark #969 detected at the Palm Beach receiver at 12:34am today (~6h ago) — the only Palm Beach→Manly detection in 24h; none at Dee Why, Long Reef, Curl Curl or Manly. Feed is current (newest statewide detection just now); ~30 real detections statewide in 24h, incl. White Shark #2979 pinging Bondi (south of Manly) through the night, and SLS drone sightings at Mollymook and One Mile Beach. DPI feed returned no features. Absence of detections at your breaks is not a guarantee — check the live map before paddling out.

days.label: Today
days.note: Best day of the week: NE/E swell mix (~430 kJ, 8s), chest high with light W/NW offshore at dawn. Glass-off window dawn–10am on the high tide, then ENE sea breeze. Go early.
days.surfline_text: It's in the chest high range for most spots from the swell mix - perhaps a bit more push at S facing with a little bit of longer S showing up more there.  Light variable to N/NW winds in the morning for cleanest window - but still expect a bit of wobble and junkiness. Then S facing as NE winds pick up.  High tide first up - head for spots that can handle some water - it's not breaking well elsewhere.
